Although DOE subsequently discontinued BP2, the project management work completed in BP1 ensured that all technical outputs were complete, documented, and ready for transition into field-demonstration planning. Overall, Task 5 provided the organizational, coordination, and schedule- management framework required for the successful completion of BP1. Through structured partner coordination, milestone tracking, risk management, and compliance with DOE reporting requirements, the project achieved the technical objectives defined in the SOPO and delivered a comprehensive, utility-grade foundation for potential future GFM demonstration activities. 7.6 Task 6 - GFM Resource and Plant-Level Control Commissioning Task 6 focused on establishing the technical, procedural, and coordination framework required for the safe commissioning of grid-forming (GFM) functions at the Wheatridge hybrid plant. In accordance with the project schedule, no field commissioning occurred during BP1. Instead, all work centered on preparing the engineering foundations necessary for future activation of GFM capabilities across the BESS, GFM wind turbines, and the plant-level supervisory controller. A primary activity under Task 6 was the development of the commissioning readiness framework, which translates the findings of EMT studies into practical field requirements. This work included defining reference-frame alignment, validating transitions between grid-following (GFL) and grid-forming (GFM) modes, identifying inverter protection and current-limiting dependencies, and determining the operational prerequisites for enabling GFM units under different system-strength conditions. These readiness elements ensure that GFM activation can occur in a controlled manner consistent with the plant’s electrical and operational characteristics. In parallel, the project team performed a plant-level interface and control-integration assessment. This activity examined how GFM inverter-level controls will interact with the plant controller, including timing behavior of reference dispatch, voltage- and frequency-control hierarchies, and supervisory-mode transitions. The review identified measurement points required for GFM enablement, assessed communication latency and signal dependencies, and clarified interactions between GFM setpoints and plant-level dispatch logic. These assessments ensured coherence between EMT-model assumptions and real plant control pathways. Task 6 also included the development and refinement of commissioning sequences. The team collaborated across PGE, GE Vernova, and NextEra to define step-by- Page 18 of 36 Award Number: DE-EE0010651 Recipient Name: Portland General Electric step activation routines, including synchronization checks, verification of voltage- reference agreements, confirmation of current-limiting thresholds, protection-setting validation, and staged enablement of GFM modes. Specific attention was given to the ordering of actions required to prevent abrupt power or angle transitions and to ensure stable controller operation during the initial GFL-to-GFM conversion. These sequences draw directly from system behaviors observed in EMT studies and reflect practical constraints at the plant. In addition, the project performed dependency and risk identification for commissioning. Highlighted the importance of understanding dependencies between inverter-level controllers, plant-level functions, SCADA pathways, and protective relaying. Task 6 captured these dependencies and documented technical risks, including weak-grid sensitivity, interaction among dissimilar inverter types, and the need for coordinated tuning across the hybrid resource fleet. Mitigation strategies were defined to address these risks ahead of field implementation. Several coordination activities were completed during BP1 to maintain alignment across project partners.
